title: Constraint-aware Rollout Navigator
creator: Aisha Fernandez
description:
Summary: Design a compact yet expressive Rollout Navigator that helps non-engineer product owners and SREs author traffic split plans constrained by budget, latency SLOs, and regulatory boundaries (e.g., region-only audiences). Goal is to reduce cognitive load when composing multi-stage canaries and A/B experiments and to surface best-effort warnings and automated suggestions.

What this ticket covers: low-fidelity -> clickable prototype -> handoff screens for the main editor canvas, constraint panel, 'safety suggestions' assistant, and rollback quick-actions. Focus areas: visualizing overlap between audience segments and regulatory constraints, encoding cost budget into ramp steps, and showing simulated traffic and expected p95 latency deltas.

Design decisions & trade-offs considered: 1) Inline versus modal constraint editor — we prototyped inline because it keeps context for complex multi-step ramps, but it adds canvas density. We mitigated by collapsible lanes and progressive disclosure. 2) Automated suggestions (e.g., scale down step size when cost budget exceeded) — we recommend non-blocking suggestions with one-click apply rather than automatic changes. 3) Simulation fidelity — a lightweight probabilistic simulator that uses historical latency and token-cost distributions provides quick feedback; we sacrificed absolute accuracy for interactivity.

Artifacts and links: PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/PRD-Console-Rollouts-V2 (internal)
Prototype (Figma clickable): https://www.figma.com/file/rollout-navigator-proto (internal)
Design spec & tokens: https://drive.redwood.com/design/console-rollouts-v2/specs (internal)
Initial evaluation dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/rollout-sim?orgId=1 (read-only)
Relevant github PRs that will consume CSS vars and component definitions: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-ui/pull/2148 and https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-ui/pull/2167

Progress so far: - 2025-02-12: Kickoff & brief with PM (Hannah Cho) and Eng (Kavya Patel). Alignment on constraints: cost budget, p95 latency target, region exclusion. - 2025-02-14: Low-fi flows completed, reviewed with PM and two SREs. Feedback: expose quick-rollback earlier and add a visual overlap inspector for audience slices. - 2025-02-17: Mid-fi prototype created, added lightweight simulator and safety suggestion chips. Conducted 3 unmoderated sessions with internal PM and support team. Observations: users expect a 'what-if' preview for rollback and for A/B to show absolute metric deltas, not only percentage splits. - 2025-02-19: Design critique with Eng and Product; Eng flagged API contract gap for simulator (needs an endpoints/sample API to fetch segment overlap matrix).

Remaining work: - Address engineering concerns: refine API contract in spec doc and add fallbacks if overlap matrix unavailable. - Finalize accessibility & keyboard nav for the canvas (especially for keyboard-driven SRE workflows). - Prepare tokens & component spec for handoff (deadline 2025-02-28).

Acceptance criteria: - Clickable prototype demonstrates authoring a 4-step canary with region constraints and cost budget warnings. - Safety suggestions are shown and apply with a single tap. - Design spec provides component variants, states, and copy for all visible prompts and warnings.

Customer impact: medium — simplifies rollout authoring for customers using Dedicated and Private deployments with strict regional constraints.

Notes for engineers: simulator endpoint should accept: audience definition (list of segment IDs), ramp steps (percentages), sample window (last 7d), and return expected token-cost delta and p95 delta per step. If service returns 503, UI must show degraded 'estimate unavailable' with a cached last-known estimate.
comments: 2025-02-14 | Hannah Cho (PM): Love the overlap inspector. Can we add a readout for expected monthly spend delta? Also: label the suggestions as 'recommended' not 'required'.

2025-02-17 | Kavya Patel (Eng): Simulator sounds good but we need a small contract doc. I'll spin up an API stub for the next demo. Also flagged: we should cap simultaneous router reconfig changes to avoid load spikes.

2025-02-18 | Satya Rao (SRE): In the prototype the rollback CTA is buried in a menu — users asked for one-click rollback. Recommend adding a top-right 'Emergency rollback' affordance that sends runbook link and starts a safe revert sequence.

2025-02-19 | Design critique notes: reduce saturation on step colors; increase hit target on chips; add keyboard shortcuts: 'r' for rollback preview, 's' to apply suggestion. Marcus to iterate and re-upload prototype by 2025-02-22.
notes: Prototype needs an accessibility pass; copy must be reviewed by legal for regulated regions language before release.
